speaker: Mr Darryl David
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether he can provide an update on the number of lifts installed at pedestrian overhead bridges across Singapore in 2021; (b) how does this number compare to the number of lifts installed in 2019 and 2020; and (c) what is the projected annual number of lifts that will be installed at pedestrian overhead bridges for the next three years.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: In 2018, LTA completed Phase 2 of its lift retrofitting programme for 41 POBs, primarily near public transport nodes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: LTA was preparing for Phase 3 of the lift retrofitting programme in 2019.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Transport (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Transport)
text: Preparatory works, such as site investigations and technical studies, have to be done before commencing construction, hence, it takes about 14 to 22 months to retrofit lifts at POBs.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also like to thank the Senior Parliamentary Secretary for his reply.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I understand that perhaps with time, the cost of installation of the lifts would come down.

speaker: Mr Darryl David (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For example, conventional lifts use a certain electrical motor and mechanism, but would hydraulic lifts, for example, be a possible solution if the cost of installation of the hydraulic lifts would be a bit more economical and, therefore, allow for the Budget to be better used to serve the same purpose?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Indeed, over the years, we have explored different or better ways of providing such facilities.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But, of course, we have to also consider the high usage and that it is cost-efficient to maintain.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The costs also include site investigations and the technical things that need to be done, apart from the actual cost of the lift per se.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: I seek the public and Members' understanding that there is still a cost involved and priority will definitely be given to areas where we can benefit more commuters with such needs.
